title: The Kettle in the Glass
status: concept-proposal (Creative Director, 2026-11-19; not approved; awaiting owner review)
hook_line: One thing in this kitchen is wrong. Find it.
first_visual: Ivy's kitchen at 3 a.m. in a slow push; the window over the sink reflects the room.

beats.visual: Slow push across the kitchen; the window over the sink reflects the room; in the reflection the kettle steams.
beats.vo: One thing in this kitchen is wrong. Find it.

beats.visual: On-screen 10-second timer over the continuing push (clip 1 extended/slowed).
Ivy shuffles in, fills a glass at the sink, and doesn't look up.
beats.vo: I came down for water. Didn't notice. Did you?

beats.visual: Highlight circles: the cold real kettle, then the reflected kettle steaming.
beats.vo: The kettle in the glass is boiling. The real one's cold.

beats.visual: Push into the reflection: a figure pours two cups and sets one at Ivy's reflected place.
beats.vo: Someone in there is making tea.

beats.visual: Key moment: the reflected figure looks up; the real kettle clicks on; moth on the tea towel.
Card: 'How fast did you find it? Comment your time.'

ending: The reflected figure looks up at Ivy's reflection; the real kettle clicks on by itself.
loop_note: Yes. The last frame (kettle steaming in reality) loops to frame 1, where the kettle now matches the reflection.

interactive_prompt.on_screen_question: ONE THING IS WRONG. FIND IT. (10 s)
interactive_prompt.comment_invite: Comment how many seconds it took you.
interactive_prompt.fairness_note: The steaming reflection is visible from frame 1. Red herrings (clock, ajar cupboard) are not claimed as the answer.

originality_review: Original spot-the-difference built on our kitchen kit. A wrong reflection is a common device; the second-kitchen tea-for-two payoff is ours. It does not copy the reflection twist in MW010.
scores_basis: Initial editorial judgement, 2026-11-19. topic_demand is an estimate linked to research/WEEKLY_TREND_REPORT.md categories, not a measurement of this concept.
concept: Spot-the-difference in Ivy's 3 a.m. kitchen. The wrong detail is in the window reflection: the reflected kettle is steaming while the real one is cold. Someone in the reflection is making tea for two, and then the real kettle clicks on.

hooks.line: One thing in this kitchen is wrong. Find it.
hooks.first_visual: Ivy's kitchen at 3 a.m. in a slow push; the window over the sink reflects the room.

hooks.line: Ten seconds. Find what's wrong before she does.
hooks.first_visual: A kitchen frame with a subtle timer.

hooks.line: The kettle in the window is boiling. The real one isn't.
hooks.first_visual: A cold kettle beside its steaming reflection.

hooks.line: Someone in the reflection is making tea.
hooks.first_visual: A reflected hand pouring two cups.
A dark window over a sink.

setting: Ivy's kitchen at night; the black window over the sink.
conflict: Ivy doesn't notice; the viewer is challenged to.
escalation: Timer, red herrings (clock, ajar cupboard), Ivy fetching water.
reveal: Highlight: the steam exists only in the reflection.
emotional_objective: Hunt, then 'it's been there all along'.
